title: Repair times at a service desk
intro:
The time to close a repair ticket at a service desk is skewed to the right: most tickets close quickly, a few take hours. Over the past year the times have had mean **μ = 12 minutes** and standard deviation **σ = 9 minutes**. Each day a supervisor averages the times of a random sample of **n = 36** tickets.

The population is not normal, but n = 36 is at least 30, so the Central Limit Theorem lets you treat x̄ as normal. Find the mean of the sampling distribution of x̄, its standard error, and the probability that a day's sample mean is **10 minutes or less**. Give the mean and standard error to two decimals and the probability to three decimals or more.

ask.prompt: Mean of the sampling distribution of x̄ (minutes)

StandardError.says: That is σ, the spread of single tickets. The standard error is the spread of the sample mean: divide σ by √n.
You divided σ by n = 36. The standard error divides by √n = 6.

AtMost.says: That is P(x̄ ≥ 10), the area to the right. "10 minutes or less" is the area to the left of z.
You divided by σ = 9, the spread of single tickets. For the mean of 36 tickets divide by the standard error, σ/√n = 1.5.

hints: The sampling distribution of x̄ is centered on the population mean: the mean of x̄ equals μ.
z = (10 − 12) / standard error, then P(x̄ ≤ 10) = Φ(z), the area to the left of z under the standard normal curve.
